_readme: Example provisioning settings file. Copy to <env>-settings.json (dev|test|acc|prd)
in this folder — one file per environment — and replace every {{PLACEHOLDER}} token.
Scripts FAIL FAST on any value that still contains {{...}} (C-TECH-031 / C-TECH-047).
This file holds per-environment IDENTIFIERS only. It must never contain secrets
(C-TECH-001): the provisioning app id and certificate thumbprint stay in the

requiredResourceAccess._comment: Least privilege only (C-TECH-043): e.g. Sites.Selected over Sites.FullControl.All. Broad permissions need a TAD §6 justification + ADR.

federatedCredentials._comment: C-TECH-044 - a federated credential (OIDC) removes the client secret entirely rather than rotating it. This is the credential .github/workflows/ci.yml uses, via `pac auth create --githubFederated`, which needs only an application id and tenant id.
federatedCredentials._comment_subject: SUBJECT THE GITHUB ENVIRONMENT, NOT A BRANCH. GitHub's OIDC `sub` claim is `repo:ORG/REPO:environment:NAME` for any job that references an environment, and only `repo:ORG/REPO:ref:refs/heads/BRANCH` for one that does not (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/oidc). Entra matches subjects as EXACT STRINGS with no wildcards, and ci.yml triggers on `feature/**`, so a branch subject would need one credential per branch name. Every authenticating job in ci.yml declares an `environment:` for exactly this reason. Replace <env> with the GitHub Environment name: dev, tst_acc or prd.
federatedCredentials._comment_one_per_registration: Declare EXACTLY ONE credential per app registration, and use a SEPARATE registration per deploy target. Several subjects on one registration would gate token ISSUANCE but not AUTHORITY: every subject resolves to the same service principal, which is an application user in every environment, so a token minted by a lower environment's job could still deploy to production. See ADR-007.
federatedCredentials.name: github-actions-env-{{GITHUB_ENVIRONMENT}}
federatedCredentials.subject: repo:{{GITHUB_ORG}}/{{GITHUB_REPO}}:environment:{{GITHUB_ENVIRONMENT}}
